newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm SIMEX, swaps boost sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firm SIMEX, swaps boost sentiment.

text.p: Firm fuel oil swaps and SIMEX futures contract boosted sentiment in the high sulphur fuel oil market on Friday, with the market strongly anticipating a local trader to continue his purchase.
The 180-cst grade was offered at $102.50 per tonne for late May delivery but there was no buyer.
The local trader on Thursday bought a 180-cst cargo from an European major at $102.00 per tonne for May 26-30 delivery, $2.00 higher than the traded level earlier this week.
The 380-cst grade, which was traded at $91.00 per tonne last week, was bid at $94.50.
"The demand is there, for bunkers or power stations, but it's so far regular and not that significant," said one trader, predicting prices to stay firm.
"Sentiment is quite bullish at the moment," he added.
Fuel oil swaps jumped on expectations of fresh physical market demand, with May rising to $103.75/$104.50 from $101.50/$102.50 and June advancing to $102/$103 from $99.50/$100.50.
"I think the cargo market is largely paper-led," said one trader.
SIMEX fuel oil futures also saw some sharp gains, with June jumping $2.00 to $102.00 and July inching up 80 cents to $100.50.
Block trades of two 5,000 lots each was also heard traded at around $93.30 on Thursday.
Most traders agreed that tighter summer supplies from the Middle East and South Korea's maintenance turnarounds in May and June did provide fundamental support for the market.
Recent fuel oil import tender from Taiwan and South Korea also boosted sentiment, traders said.
Taiwan's state Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Friday it had bought two 38,000-tonne cargoes of 0.5-percent fuel oil at around $117 and $120 per tonne respectively.

The Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) has tendered to buy two 70,000-tonne, 540-centistoke fuel oil for July delivery. The tender for 0.3-percent fuel oil will close on May 16 and is valid for three days.
